hits.text:
this is the most successful launch video in Silicon Valley history

18 years ago, the founder of Dropbox recorded his screen to make this demo

it took their waitlist from 5,000 to 75,000 overnight

imo, here's what made it work:

1. it showed the real product doing the one thing it promised. you drop a file into a folder and it shows up on your other computer

2. it was full of inside jokes for the exact audience he was trying to reach

3. he posted it where his users already were. an earlier version went on Hacker News, and this one went on Digg

4. it explained a new idea without any jargon

5. it let people see something they couldn't use yet. Dropbox wasn't open to the public, so the video showed it working and the waitlist did the rest

while everyone is doing super fancy video with Claude, you can do a very simple screen recording 

you will look x10 more authentic

The era of System One Vision Model is here! Introducing VFlash: parsing the visual world in parallel at unmatched speeds for Physical AI.

Most embodied prediction tasks like object localization, robot trajectory planning, and dense 3D motion are fixed-length float vectors. For example, a bounding box is always 6 tokens, a 10-waypoint robot arm trajectory is 54: we know these beforehand. Instead of decoding one token at a time, we can output the entire geometric shape in one go.

trend_radar.legend: Trend match 0-100% = 1 - prod(1 - w) over matched 24 h keywords that another author also used in the 48 h window (w: rank 1-10 0.35, 11-25 0.22, 26-40 0.12, curated 0.20). Verdict: >= 50% -> trend; else video/image in the post data -> visual; else >= 100K followers (outsiders without follower data: >= 500K views, estimate) -> author/audience; else coincidence/other. Missing data shows as 'no data'. Heat = sum log10(views) of topic posts (24 h x1, 24-48 h x0.5), scaled to 100. Momentum = log-views last 24 h / previous 24 h. Trend-input-only accounts feed the corpus but are never shown as hits.
